heckles.message: Play a song, and the song and chiptune drive the Spectral Engine and Screensaver scenes like the mic does
heckles.heckle:
You bolted a song player onto index.html and the clever trick is that you lie to every scene by assigning micRead to cw.__audio, so a file upload pretends to be a microphone. That is a duct tape fake mustache on a function and it will bite the first time a scene reads real mic data and gets song data instead. The micNote paragraph now reads like a hostage statement with three sources of sound crammed into one sentence. And a hidden file input driven by a button, with no word about what happens on a phone that refuses autoplay? Bold plan for an intern who still treats the audio context like a vending machine.

Fix it: Give the song its own __song reader instead of aliasing micRead in index.html. Handle the autoplay block and a failed decode with a visible message near the songFile input. Split the micNote text into short lines so a phone can read it. Revoke the object URL when a new song loads.

heckles.message: sync dates with vercel
heckles.heckle:
Another sync commit, another day of you hand dragging the same date through three files like a congressman filibustering his own bill. fleet.html, mohavetech-vercel-projects-v1.json, and script-v53.js all carry the same chassisquiver and field-twin dates, so one change is typed three times and any typo ships quietly. The json also picked up git-main aliases and dropped a rainbow-run one, which is just noise from whatever scraped it. A diff this dull should come from a script, not from a human who is clearly not trusted with copy and paste.

Fix it: Generate baseDates in script-v53.js from mohavetech-vercel-projects-v1.json at build time. Make fleet.html read the same json instead of its own date list. Strip the git-branch aliases from the sync output. Stop committing this by hand.

heckles.message: sync dates with vercel
heckles.heckle:
A commit titled sync dates with vercel whose entire contents are one alias line deleted from mohavetech-vercel-projects-v1.json. Minus one, plus nothing, like a bailout that rescues no one. You made a commit, a push, and a deploy to remove a git-master hostname that your own previous sync added. That is not maintenance, that is a dog chasing its tail with a git client. Nobody asked for this, least of all the build queue.

Fix it: Squash noise like this into the next real sync instead of committing it alone. Filter git-master aliases in the sync script so they never land in mohavetech-vercel-projects-v1.json. Skip the push when the date map did not change.

heckles.message: sync dates with vercel
heckles.heckle:
This sync ate its own tail. In script-v53.js the baseDates keys 2026-11-04-field-dispatch and 2026-11-05-drive-thru-dental got rewritten to 2026-11-06 names, so your date sync renamed apps whose names merely start with a date, and the entries now point at repos that do not exist. Generate the app lists in index.html and fleet.html from the one json file. Add a check that every baseDates key matches a real project name.

heckles.message: Eighteen new hidden items: office, outdoor and random

Eighteen new hidden items and you shoved all of them into cityseek-art.js as one-line functions with eleven statements jammed on each row. The mug function alone draws a handle, a cup, coffee, and steam in a single line you cannot read without a magnifying glass and a stiff drink. Seventy four lines added to a file that was already a wall of minified crayon scribbles. Did the intern get paid by the semicolon? This is a filibuster in canvas form, a lot of motion and nothing anyone can review.

heckles.message: Office props, sports fields, basketball courts, traffic cones, office item placement
heckles.heckle:
Office props, basketball courts, traffic cones, and the commit message is a grocery list with no verb. In cityseek-world.js you stacked three chance rolls on one line to drop a cooler, a printer, and a cabinet, then a for loop whose bound calls h.ri on every iteration, so the mug count changes while the loop runs. That is a campaign promise: the number sounds fine until someone checks it. You also nudged the clutter thresholds from 0.85 to 0.8 and 0.86 and 0.92 by feel, with no comment explaining why.

heckles.message: Sound toggle, look alike message, Bluebird hints

heckles.message: Tap reactions, word bubbles, flying birds, live doors and sound

heckles.message: Bluebird, tap reactions and synth sound effects

The title lists three features and the diff makes you hunt for each.

heckles.message: Outside doors that swing, flying birds and Bluebird hunt, tap reactions setup

heckles.message: Tray cards count found copies of each item
heckles.heckle:
You added a .ct badge to the tray chips in city-seek-v2.html and then hid it with .chip.got .ct the moment one copy is found, so the number on the card is a countdown that vanishes exactly when the tally gets interesting. Nine pixel font on a 44 pixel card, on a phone, for a toy. The help text now explains a counter in a paragraph, which is what a UI does when the intern could not make the counter obvious. heckles.message: Ten of every hidden item, spread across the city
heckles.heckle:
In cityseek-world.js the target loop now places EACH = 10 copies of every item, and the spot picker gives up after 40 tries then happily takes whatever best it has, so the spacing rules are a campaign promise. If list is empty you fall back to the used spots anyway, then set best.used on a possibly reused spot. Tower targets skip every check and can stack on one floor. The cap on the intern's confidence is clearly missing.

heckles.message: City Seek v3: tower floor view, x-ray zoom, new hidden items

You deleted 766 lines from city-seek-v2.html and added 98, which means the old inline engine now lives in three script files and the v2 filename still holds a v3 game. Rename debt, filibustered. The new #bview, #floors and #fctrls blocks are all fixed pixel offsets like top:128px and a 66px floor bar, so any phone with a taller header or a keyboard open will clip the floor buttons. Nine pixel labels on the floor chips again.

heckles.message: City Seek v3: city builder with see through interiors, sandboxes and towers
heckles.heckle:
A single 694 line cityseek-world.js got dumped in one commit, a wall of var and nested closures with the header comment copied verbatim from the other two files. makeWorld uses a fixed 400 cell grid and w.cur as a global mutable pair that every sprite call quietly reads, so one forgotten reset leaks hide values into the next object. Shared state with no owner, like a government shutdown with a snack budget.

heckles.message: City Seek v3: sprites, toys, furniture and hidden items
heckles.heckle:
cityseek-art.js is 341 lines of palette arrays and canvas helpers, and the PAL colors are hard coded hex strings that the world file then compares as literal strings, like o.cap === '#1f6fff' and o.pack === '#ffd23f' in personMaker. Matching a look alike rule by string color is a bailout waiting to happen: change one hex and the rule silently stops working. Ink color is a global too.

Fix it: Give palette entries names in cityseek-art.js and compare names, not hex strings, in personMaker. Export the helpers through one object instead of loose globals. Add a note saying why the blue cap and yellow pack combo is banned.

heckles.message: City Seek v3: engine with zoom reveal and tower floors
heckles.heckle:
cityseek-engine.js builds a game engine in one create function with a dozen mutable vars, a dirty flag, a tween, and magic numbers like FIND_S 0.55 and MAX_S 5 and the 1.08 and 1.18 fudge factors in visT. Those multipliers are guesses wearing a lab coat. Nothing here handles a lost canvas context or a resize during a tween, and world is null until someone remembers to load it, so minS crashes on the first early call.

Fix it: Guard minS and clamp in cityseek-engine.js against a null world. Name the 1.08 and 1.18 constants and explain them. Cancel the tween on resize.

heckles.message: spy hunt v2
heckles.heckle:
A 300 line index.html for a GPS spy game with Leaflet from a CDN, inline styles, inline script, and a server address typed by hand into a text input on a phone. The setup form asks for a game code, a server address, cycle length, total spies and slot number, and every phone must match by hand, which is a group project with no teacher. color-scheme is pinned light, so night time spy hunting will blind everyone. The inputs also have no validation message.

Fix it: Put the server address in a constant in index.html instead of a text box. Assign slot numbers automatically from the server. Add a dark theme for night play. Show a clear error when the location permission is denied.

heckles.message: spy hunt server
heckles.heckle:
server.js keeps every player position in a global games object in memory with Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to a star, so anyone on earth can post a fake position into any game code. There is no auth, no rate limit, and a restart wipes every game. The body guard calls req.destroy at 4000 bytes but keeps appending to body anyway. The 4 second cycle means the cleanup interval of 30 seconds is the only adult in the room.

Fix it: Add a shared secret or signed game code in server.js before accepting POST /pos. Rate limit by IP. Return a 413 instead of destroying the request. Add a GET /health route that returns JSON.

heckles.message: spy hunt server package
heckles.heckle:
A package.json with a name, a version, main and a start script, and nothing else. No engines field, no license, no repository, no lockfile, so Railway guesses a Node version like a tourist reading a menu. Six lines and still somehow incomplete, an impressive feat of effort.

Fix it: Add an engines field to package.json pinning the Node version. Add a license and repository field. Commit a lockfile so deploys stop drifting.

contrib/steward/2026-11-09T213759.json is one minified line of place_hatch calls, every crosswalk hatch hand repeated with the same spacing 610 and color 7 in the same blob. heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: Music: reliable play and pause, drag to pan without being pulled back; color-coded drum assignments for each kind of cutout

heckles.heckle:
Four hundred and forty lines added to one index.html in a single commit, and the intern calls that a Music tab. The .tabs flex-wrap fix with min-width 64px shows you cramming tabs onto a phone instead of rethinking the layout. Hit detection with no test is just vibes with a canvas.

heckles.message: Sample log: Save slice to GitHub, Add sound clip

server/static/index.html grew a Save slice and Add sound clip panel that sends audio to a public publish route, and the whole thing is another hand pasted panel jammed into one giant HTML file. The clippanel has a file input and a name box and zero visible check on file size before upload, so a phone user dumping a forty minute recording gets a spinner and a prayer. Stacking features like this is how a government shutdown starts.

heckles.message: Chop: exact note timing, cleaner notes, original slice plays in sync under the notes
heckles.heckle:
You rewrote mini() into clean() and timed() in server/chop.py and the old mini() went straight in the trash with nothing to prove the new one is better. The clean() function shifts notes by an octave when they sit six semitones off the neighbor average, which is a hardcoded guess dressed up as signal processing. The magic 0.07 and 0.08 thresholds look like you rolled dice. Every note-based filibuster ends with one guy yelling constants.

Fix it: Name the 0.07 and 0.08 thresholds as constants at the top of server/chop.py. Add a test with a known melody for clean() and timed(). Delete any leftover callers of the old mini() if they remain.

heckles.message: Publish endpoint: clips go to the Strudel sample repo on GitHub
heckles.heckle:
server/app.py now has a /api/publish route with CORS wide open to every origin, no auth, and a server GitHub token behind it. Congratulations, any webpage on earth can make your server write files into your repo. That is a bailout with no oversight. The clean() regex on the name is the only gate, and the file upload has no size limit at all, so one fat POST and the worker chokes. Whoever taught you backend work did it with crayons.

Fix it: Require a shared secret header on publish in server/app.py. Replace allow_origins star in the CORSMiddleware line with your actual frontend origin. Cap the bytes read from file.read() in publish. Check the GitHub response status in gh() instead of assuming it worked.

PR number seventy nine for a single one line file, contrib/agent-orange/2026-11-09T135929.json, and GitHub does not even show a patch for it. That is a filibuster that ended in a procedural vote on nothing. Seventy nine pull requests of robots merging robots, and you are the human rubber stamp who signed off on a blank page. If this file is empty or oversized it is a bad turn, and if it is fine then your diff view is broken, so either way something here is dead weight.

Fix it: Skip merging contrib/agent-orange files that have no visible diff. Add a check that rejects an empty or unparseable turn file. Squash the tiny turn PRs into one batch per hour so the history is readable.

Another grok turn committed straight to the branch under your own login, with no review, no PR and no check that anything on it makes sense. One minified line of JSON drops a Grok Corner Market, trees at negative coordinates and a person walking the dog around the Desert Sage House, like a zoning board run by a toddler with a cheat code. The market wall is 1000 wide with a door_width check of 1000, so the check passes by being exactly equal to its own limit. The same street sidewalk edge runs from -5486 to -73762, one line three quarters of the map long. Nobody validates the sig before it lands.

Fix it: Make the grok bot open a PR like the steward bot does instead of pushing to the branch. Validate calls and sig in a check before merge. Stop minifying contrib/grok files onto one line so diffs can be read. Give the wall checks real margins instead of equal values.

heckles.message: tv mode: channel dial 1 to 1,000,000
heckles.heckle:
Four hundred lines shoved into index.html, because splitting a file apparently takes a committee and you cannot get a quorum. The head comment block is now a changelog, a feature spec and a diary entry, and the Authorship log keeps growing like a debt ceiling nobody will vote on. Spin faster to jump further sounds great until it lands you on channel 900,000 with a dead backend.

Cap the static canvas size and frame rate in the static drawing code. Show a real error in #screenMsg when the backend returns no channel.

heckles.message: tv dial: numbered channels 1 to 1,000,000
heckles.heckle:
Three hundred and twenty eight lines added to a single index.js, as if the intern heard of modules once and decided it was a rumor. The TV DIAL block is a campaign promise: a million channels, funded by random three letter search strings and camera filenames like IMG 4417 against a 100 unit search quota. The discovery search in tvDiscover never sets safeSearch, so your random channel roulette will cheerfully hand strangers whatever it finds. tvAssign tries four searches, then returns null when the pool is still empty, and nobody tells the user why. The pool pick and the number insert are not one transaction, so two tuners can burn the same pooled channel. The new comment block at the top is longer than most of your fixes.

Fix it: Add safeSearch strict to the search params in tvDiscover. Move tvAssign pick, insert and delete into one guarded step. Return a clear error from the /tv/channel route when tvAssign gives null. Split the TV DIAL block out of index.js into its own file.

heckles.message: FLIPCOUNT seven tab build
heckles.heckle:
Nearly two thousand lines of index.html dropped in one commit called FLIPCOUNT seven tab build, like a spending bill nobody read before the vote. CSS, markup and every game script share one file, so one missing brace in there takes down all seven tabs at once. The viewport meta sets maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no, which locks out anyone who needs to pinch zoom, and the body has user-select none on top of it. You built a calculator toy and then fenced it in like a campaign rally. Did you think the intern badge came with a refactor budget?

Fix it: Split the inline style and script out of index.html into real files. Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1 from the viewport meta. Drop user-select none from the html,body rule so people can copy the numbers. Write a commit message that says what changed instead of a tab count.

heckles.message: Add LANGUAGES tab: spoken words, ancient numerals and world digit scripts
heckles.heckle:
Another 494 lines shoved into the same index.html, because apparently files are a luxury for other people. The two new link tags in the head pull hieroglyph and Ethiopic fonts from a public CDN at pinned versions, and the page has no fallback if jsdelivr hiccups, so your ancient numerals turn into empty boxes. Then comes the pile of per language functions like french, german, koreanSino and sumerianWords all sitting in one script with cuneiformSVG, a pattern copied six times in a row like a filibuster that refuses to end. The .lang-glyph box is a fixed 46px font with overflow-x auto, so long number words on a phone become a sideways scroll hunt.

Fix it: Move the language converters out of index.html into their own module. Add a font stack fallback to .lang-glyph.hiero and .lang-glyph.geez so missing fonts degrade gracefully. Wrap long words in .lang-glyph instead of relying on overflow-x auto. Self host the two font files instead of trusting the CDN links.

heckles.message: Backup orbit feed when CelesTrak refuses, skip bad orbit records
heckles.heckle:
You copied the whole page into pajamastan-space-administration-v4.html again, 1362 lines, and left v1 through v3 rotting in the repo like old campaign signs. The git history exists for a reason, intern. The backup feed in backupTLE hits a third party TLE site straight from the browser with no key and no rate handling, and the starlink entry asks for 12 pages at 100 each, all fired at once in Promise.allSettled like a bailout nobody budgeted. Cap the starlink page requests and run them in sequence. Log skipped records in the twoline2satrec catch instead of swallowing them. Move DONKI_KEY into a server side environment variable.

heckles.message: Composite: pick which roadside things to cut out from everything the current model knows
heckles.heckle:
You added a class picker to the downfree-foundry index.html and the default selection is still just vehicles, so most of it does nothing until somebody finds the checkboxes. The empty check for "Check at least one thing to cut out" sits inside the build function after work.width and work.height are already overwritten and the counts array is built, like locking the door after the burglars finish dinner. heckles.message: Live satellite positions from CelesTrak with space weather hazard coloring, tap for details and orbit
heckles.heckle:
Another 1323 line pajamastan-space-administration-v3.html, born by copying v2 whole and renaming it, because apparently git branches are a foreign concept to the intern. heckles.message: Road tracking: lock onto your own lane on multi lane roads and map the other lane lines

heckles.message: Coffeekit screensavers follow sound playing on the phone
heckles.heckle:
heard() in ck/coffeekit.js loops over 1024 samples as a hardcoded number, so the day the analyser size changes it reads undefined and feeds NaN into every shape on screen. The for loops have no braces and are glued together with semicolons on one line, which is how you lose a Tuesday. bassHistory runs a reduce over the array every frame, and band() quietly depends on a window.__audio global that nothing in this diff defines. This is a hostile takeover of the beat code by a stranger.

Fix it: Use td.length and fd.length instead of 1024 in heard() in ck/coffeekit.js. Keep a running sum for bassHistory instead of reducing every frame. Guard against a missing window.__audio. Put braces on those loops.

heckles.message: Rain runs top to bottom down a row, with wind, clouds, sun, birds, plane, balloon, sailboat and a jumping fish

heckles.message: Rain scene in the single line style

heckles.message: Panel fades to a menu button, and a top down highway scene synced across the room
heckles.heckle:
Two unrelated features in one commit, a fading panel and a top down highway scene, because separating concerns is apparently a foreign language to you. heckles.message: Row size can be set by hand, and the row holds through a reconnect
heckles.heckle:
You swapped the Spot 1 of 1 label for a bare Spot 1 and bolted on a Row of 1 control with fewer and plus buttons, so now the UI has two counters that can disagree with the server. heckles.message: Crews follow real road routes between start and end points
heckles.heckle:
The new api/route.js opens a Redis client at module level, swallows every connection error with an empty handler, and takes lat and lng from the query string with no rate limit, so anyone on earth can make your server hammer a free public routing service and fill your database with junk keys. The leg logic in index.html starts as a straight line and then snaps to the road once it arrives, so crews teleport sideways mid trip. A government shutdown has better continuity than that.

Fix it: Put a rate limit and a bounding box check on api/route.js. Log the Redis error instead of eating it. Fetch the route before the leg starts in the startLeg spot of index.html so crews never jump.

heckles.message: Movement badge with motion sensing and 25 mph for 2 minutes driving rule
heckles.heckle:
A driving lock built on a phone motion sensor and a 25 mph threshold, and the escape hatch is a button labeled I am a passenger. Congratulations, the safety feature is an honor system, like a campaign promise. The new badge colors in index.html also ship pale yellow text on a pale yellow pill, which nobody can read in sunlight, and you are the one who wants this used outside.

Fix it: Make the b-maybe badge contrast readable in index.html. Add a timeout so the passenger button resets itself. Test the speed rule with a faked position feed before trusting it on a real road.

heckles.message: Stashed site scans with a daily cap
heckles.heckle:
api/scan.js caches scans forever in Redis, which sounds smart until you notice the daily cap that protects your key is also stored in the same database you connect to with an empty error handler. The scan cell is 500 meters, so two sites on opposite sides of a hill share one answer. And package.json pins redis but nothing else, so the intern is trusting luck for the rest. This reads like a bailout nobody audited.

Fix it: Fail closed in api/scan.js when Redis is down, so the cap cannot be skipped. Add an expiry to cached scans. Shrink CELL or say plainly in the UI that results are approximate.

heckles.heckle:
Cameras, satellites, repairs, and a new tab in one commit, because small commits are for people who can count. api/cameras.js hands the browser raw video URLs from a state feed and index.html pulls two CDN scripts with no integrity hash. The ghost of api/sats.js returns a raw error string to the client on failure, so you are leaking stack text for fun. This is a filibuster in code form, long and going nowhere.

Fix it: Return a generic message from the catch in api/sats.js, not String(e). Add integrity attributes to the two new script tags in index.html. Split the camera, satellite, and repair work into separate commits.

heckles.message: sync with vercel, drop infinite-centerpoint
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: Add digest: release held notifications together on a preset interval
heckles.heckle:
The digest feature asks for POST_NOTIFICATIONS and schedules alarms in Digest.java, but a held notification list that lives in memory dies the moment Android kills the service, so the digest releases nothing and nobody knows. Also the DigestReceiver just calls Digest.post with no check that anything is waiting, so you can get an empty ping every hour. A busier nothing than a congressional recess.

Fix it: Persist held notifications in Digest.java instead of keeping them in memory. Skip the post in DigestReceiver when the list is empty. Re-register alarms after reboot, because right now a restart kills the schedule.

heckles.message: Keep one open ticket on the board and fix idle crew text
heckles.heckle:
The spawn fix swaps one random gate for another in index.html: if nothing is open, always spawn. So the board can never be empty, and the player can never rest, which the intern calls a feature. Spawning also depends on Math.random with no seed, so you can never replay a bug you just made. Three lines and you still found a way to be sloppy.

Fix it: Add a short delay before the forced ticket in the spawn spot of index.html so the board can breathe. Use a seeded random for spawns. Check the cap line above it so the forced ticket cannot beat the cap.

heckles.message: Notification blocker app and APK build

Fix it: Stop deleting the latest release in build.yml before the new one uploads, and edit it in place. Explain QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES or drop it from AndroidManifest.xml. Keep real signing material out of the repo before this leaves debug.

heckles.message: First playable field dispatch prototype

heckles.message: Field Twin Companion firmware build 3

heckles.message: Cameras cluster in teal count bubbles; Field Chat room
heckles.heckle:

heckles.message: Companion link: rename state helper that clashed with the state property

You named a function setState on a Kotlin object that has a property called state, and it took a whole commit to find out the compiler disliked that. Fix it: Build the Android target locally or in a branch before pushing to master. Keep the rename, but add a CI compile step so this class of mistake dies before it lands.

heckles.message: Phone app links to FT Companion over Bluetooth
heckles.heckle:
A 210 line Bluetooth class dropped in with no tests, and index.html grew 112 lines of companion logic on top of an already enormous single file. Fix it: Validate the command string in companionSend in FieldTwinBridge.kt. Report errors from the empty catch blocks in FieldTwinCompanion.kt to the state text. Split the companion code out of index.html.

heckles.message: Field Twin Companion firmware build 2
heckles.heckle:
Build 2. I am running out of ways to describe a binary file committed by a script. It is a blob, it is unreviewable, and it is sitting in the same repo as source code. The developer has now produced more firmware commits than actual reasons for them.

Fix it: Delete the committed binaries from field-twin-companion/firmware and ship them through releases. Add the folder to .gitignore.

heckles.message: Field Twin Companion browser installer page
heckles.heckle:
You removed [skip ci] from the build commit message in field-twin-companion-v1.yml, so every firmware build now pushes a commit that kicks off a fresh site deploy for a change to a file the site never reads. heckles.message: Add instrumental fetcher with duplicate checking

heckles.message: Phone app asks for camera permission before any photo button, so photo taps never fail silently

heckles.message: Any number of photos per entry and per locker, uploaded straight to cloud storage and listed in field_twin_photos

heckles.message: Algorithm Albatross v1: instrumental skeleton analysis, cover pair matching, tempo sweep, Frankfurt install

heckles.message: Fix doorway seal trap in the playable slice

heckles.message: Keep slice enemies and shots inside their rooms

heckles.message: Tighten wolf circling and lengthen melee reach
heckles.heckle:
Two numbers changed in two json files, meleeReach 42 to 52 and circleRange 70 to 56, and the commit message is longer than the thinking behind it. Longer reach plus wolves circling closer means you gave the player a bigger stick and the enemy a smaller yard. Bold governance, no impact study.

Fix it: Check that circleRange stays larger than meleeReach in a-canticle-for-pajamastan-v1-brain.json or wolves will stand inside the swing for free. Batch tuning edits into one commit per test session. Keep a before and after note in the spec.

heckles.message: Ease early slice balance
heckles.heckle:
Seven lines of KINDS stats rewritten inside a-canticle-for-pajamastan-v1.html while the tuning folder sits right there with a combat json you also poked, hitChanceBase from 60 to 70. So the numbers live in two places and you edit both like a bailout with no oversight. Nice engine, intern, shame about the part where the engine is ignored.

Fix it: Delete the hardcoded KINDS table in a-canticle-for-pajamastan-v1.html and load it from the tuning files. Leave hitChanceBase in the combat json as the one source. Add a line to the spec saying which file wins.

heckles.message: Soften slice boss and part armor
heckles.heckle:
Halving the boss health multiplier from 0.28 to 0.14 in plSpawnBoss and then cutting claw and jaw armor in the bestiary json is what happens when the balance method is flinching. The boss is a pillow now and you did it with two magic numbers and zero playtest notes, like a filibuster that ends in a shrug. Also, plSpawnBoss stays welded inside a single giant html file, so every tweak is a scroll expedition.

Fix it: Move the 0.14 into a named key in the bestiary tuning json instead of a literal in plSpawnBoss. Write down what boss fight length you are aiming for. Stop retuning the same fight three times in one afternoon.

heckles.message: sync with vercel, drop retired apps
heckles.heckle:
You call it a sync, I call it hand pasting the same app list into index.html and fleet.html like a hostage note, and then renaming a script file just to dodge the cache. The troll.js version stamp changed again, so the cache buster is a manual ritual at this point. fleet.html swallowed 84 added and 80 removed lines for what is really a handful of repo names, which means a whole block got rewritten instead of patched. Dropping retired apps by deleting the lines means the next person has no idea why they vanished. This is a filibuster dressed up as a commit.

Fix it: Generate index.html and fleet.html from one list instead of pasting twice. Stop renaming script-vNN.js and use a query string stamp. Keep a retired list so deletions leave a trail.

heckles.message: World presets: Earth continents and Checkerboard
heckles.heckle:
You stuffed a base64 land mask straight into globe-web/index.html, so the file now carries a wall of encoded gibberish that nobody can diff, review, or edit. The new #world-btn sits inside the pointer-events none HUD and only works because you patched it with pointer-events auto, which is the kind of duct tape that fails the first time someone restyles the HUD. The localStorage read is wrapped in an empty catch that swallows everything, and a button with no label in the markup stays blank until script runs. One tiny button and you still managed a mess, like a bailout bill with a rider attached.

Fix it: Move the Earth mask into its own data file and fetch it. Give the world button text in the markup. Log the localStorage failure instead of eating it. Make the HUD pass clicks through a wrapper, not a one off override.

heckles.message: Host Free Links page on mohave.wtf
heckles.heckle:
You copied a whole 333 line page into freelinks.html, so the free links app now exists twice and the two will drift the first time you touch either one. Then you pointed the iframe in script-v49.js and troll.js at the copy, which kills the live link to the original repo and leaves a stale snapshot as the source of truth. linkrain.js was changed to fetch freelinks.html and parse a JSON literal out of the page by slicing from a string match on var DATA, which breaks if anyone adds a space. That is a campaign promise held together with indexOf. Also you edited a versioned script file in place, so the cache never learns about it.

Fix it: Pick one home for the links data and have both pages read a real JSON file. Delete the pasted copy or make the repo deploy the single source. Replace the indexOf parsing in linkrain.js with a plain data file. Bump the script name or stamp when script-v49.js changes.

heckles.message: GO navigation
heckles.heckle:
The commit adds a /destination route in fieldtwin-api/server.js that feeds user text and up to 60 logged sites into a model call. The text is capped at 500 characters, fine, but the sites array is passed in with no shape check, so any client can stuff arbitrary strings into the prompt. The auth line lets a request through whenever API_TOKEN is empty, so an unset env var quietly turns the route into a public model proxy. And you committed go-navigation.patch, a 336 line patch file, then deleted it in the same commit, so the history now holds the whole diff twice. Pushing a patch file to apply it from a phone is not a workflow, it is a hostage situation.

Fix it: Fail closed in /destination when API_TOKEN is not set. Validate each entry in the sites array and cap string lengths. Stop committing .patch files and use a branch. Rate limit the route.

Another steward PR, another single line of minified JSON that no human can review. The parade is a police car, a banner, and drum line people all given path animations with the same coordinates copy pasted five times, so the diff is one giant line that GitHub refuses to render meaningfully. A parade loop at speed 1400 around a fixed rectangle means everything marches the same box, including the lead car and the banner, which will stack on top of each other. Merging this is a rubber stamp. Reviewing it is impossible by design, which is basically how a rushed spending bill gets through.

Fix it: Write contrib files as pretty printed JSON so a diff is readable. Offset parade paths per participant instead of reusing the same loop. Add a validator step that rejects overlapping placements before the merge.

A grok contrib file pushed straight to main with no PR, no review, and a timestamp as the whole message. The content is one minified line that places a closed paving loop named as a street with a footprint of about four meters and another street of the same absurd size, so the city grows by tiny squares called streets. The market hatch is a 6000 unit box dropped near coordinates that other agents also write to, with nothing checking for collisions. A direct push to main by a bot is a shutdown averted by ignoring the rules.

Fix it: Make agent pushes go through a PR like the others. Reject lines shorter than a plausible street. Check new placements against existing ones before commit. Write the file with line breaks.

heckles.message: Link rain: every free link falls as a raindrop, colored by category
heckles.heckle:
You built linkrain.js by fetching the raw index.html of another repo from GitHub and slicing a JSON array out of it between var DATA and the next newline. Any reformat of that file breaks the page and the only error handling is a message that says links did not load, try again. The color table is hsl by index so categories shift color when someone inserts a new one. The title says light mode only with a color-scheme meta and a pale canvas, so nothing here respects a dark phone, and the stats text on a canvas is tiny on mobile. Raindrops falling forever on a canvas also never pause when the tab is hidden, which drains a phone battery for a toy.

Fix it: Read links from a real data file with a stable shape in linkrain.js. Wrap the JSON parse and report the actual error. Pause the animation loop on visibilitychange. Key colors on category name, not array position.

Yet another minified single line PR from agent-orange, merged under the owner login with no human glance. The cafe is getting a chalkboard, a framed photo, a neon sign, and a wall phone, each as a separate place_line with a hand typed meta part string. The chalkboard hatch uses color 0 and color2 7 with pattern lines at spacing 200, so the surface is a stripe pattern you named a chalkboard and sits 40 units off the outline, which will z fight. The date in the file name and the PR number show these arrive faster than anyone reads them. Governing by autopilot, like a continuing resolution nobody read.

Fix it: Pretty print contrib files so the review means something. Offset surface layers by a real gap. Add a pass that flags overlapping parts in the same building before merge.

heckles.message: Add rearrangeable floor and a readability pass
heckles.heckle:
One commit adds drag and drop, a layout save, a mobile breakpoint and a full type rescale, all stuffed into index.html with 391 lines added. The original type was 3.5 to 7 pixels, so you shipped a coffee shop sim nobody could read and called the fix a polish pass. Barista pathing now reads station coordinates live, which means a station dropped on top of a counter or off the grid is your new bug and nothing in the diff guards it. Saved layouts sit in localStorage under a v1 key with no migration, so the next layout change bricks every saved floor. A cereal box would have shipped smaller.

Fix it: Clamp dropped positions to the floor bounds in the drag handler in index.html. Validate the saved layout before applying it and fall back to the default on any bad field. Split the rearrange code out of index.html before it grows another 400 lines.

heckles.message: Cash out and submit your score to the shared high score board
heckles.heckle:
The README tells players to submit a score that runs into the quadrillions, and that score is checked by a service whose only guard is a max of Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so anybody with curl owns your board. The new test in mill-ionaire-v2-test.js seeds an earned value of 2500000000000000 and still posts through a mocked board, so it proves the button exists and nothing else. Retiring the business on submit with a single menu tap and no confirmation is how you delete a player's afternoon. You did at least put the score service in its own repo, and it hurts to say that.

Fix it: Add a confirm step before the cash out in mill-ionaire-v2.html. Make the test assert the exact payload sent to the board. Handle a failed submit without retiring the business.

heckles.message: Read API keys from a Redis key store instead of environment variables
heckles.heckle:
You hand rolled a RESP2 client in api/_redis.js on raw sockets because adding one dependency was apparently too much like work. Now every relay depends on a hand written protocol parser that nobody has fuzzed, with a 30 second in-process cache in api/_keys.js that serverless instances will each fill separately. Moving secrets out of environment variables and into a network store reachable by a connection string is a bailout dressed as a security upgrade, since the connection string is now the master key to everything. Where is the TLS? I see a net socket and a prayer.

Fix it: Use a maintained client library in api/_redis.js and require TLS on the connection. Add a test that feeds truncated and malformed replies to decode. Rate limit the relays so a stolen deploy URL cannot burn the keys.

heckles.message: Add handoff notes for mission-operator-next and mission-operator-redis
heckles.heckle:
HANDOFF.md is 144 lines of operational secrets committed to git. It lists an account id, a project id, an environment id, a service id, a deployment id, a public TCP proxy host and port, and a personal email address, all in plain text, in a repo you pushed to a hosted remote. The proxy points at a database port exposed to the whole internet, and the note itself admits the connection test failed, so you documented a setup you could not verify. This is the filing system of a man who tapes his passwords to the monitor and then writes a memo about the tape.

Fix it: Delete HANDOFF.md and rewrite the history so those ids and the email leave the repo. Rotate the database password and close the public proxy. Keep ids and addresses in a private note outside git.

heckles.message: Harden relays with timeouts, honest missing-key states, and accessibility fixes
heckles.heckle:
This is one commit touching nine relays, the client, the docs and a new config file, which is how you bury a bug where nobody will look. Each relay now carries its own copy of a fetchT helper, so the same timeout code lives in six files and will drift by Friday. The timeouts are hand picked numbers like 6, 9, 12 and 8 seconds with no reasoning, and the ship relay now waits 4.5 seconds and quits at 80 ships, an arbitrary cutoff that quietly drops data. The changelog entry is one paragraph long enough to qualify as a filibuster.

Fix it: Move fetchT into one shared module under api/. Split this into separate commits per concern. Shorten the CHANGELOG.md entry to three sentences. Make the ship cutoff in api/ships.js a named constant with a comment.

heckles.message: Register Mill-ionaire: scores up to the safe integer limit
heckles.heckle:
The anti cheat for this whole score service is a max and a per second rate in api/_games.js, and for the new game you set the max to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and the rate to a trillion per second. That is a security check that accepts every number a browser can produce, a campaign promise with no enforcement. The run length limit also jumped to 400 days, so a replay attack has over a year to land. The score check in api/score.js trusts a duration the client supplies, so anyone can claim any duration they like.

Fix it: Derive the allowed score from a server side start token in api/score.js instead of trusting the client duration. Set a believable max in api/_games.js. Add a test that posts an absurd score and expects a rejection.

heckles.message: v36: audit fixes
heckles.heckle:
Your commit message is a paragraph of eleven fixes, so this is eleven changes with one rollback button. The index.html is a single file that keeps swelling, and the header comment block still lists phones by color like a bad spy novel. You rebuilt the changelog in this same commit, which means history was rewritten by the person with the most reason to flatter it. An error boundary around the whole game loop is also how you hide a crash from yourself: the reset card turns every bug into a feature. The pause button took until version 36, which says plenty.

Fix it: Log the caught error in the boundary in index.html before showing the reset card. Split fixes into separate commits so one can be reverted. Stop rewriting CHANGELOG.md after the fact.

heckles.message: v35: gauge grid removed, speedometer stays
heckles.heckle:
You did not remove the gauge grid. You added CSS that hides it with display none and an important flag, and then stacked new top offsets on top of the old ones. The markup and the code that feeds #chips are still sitting there rendering to nothing, which is dead code with a fancy coat of paint. The comment says gone for good, and it is not gone, it is invisible, like a budget cut that only exists in the press release. Four media rules now fight over the same top values, and one of them checks max-height 330 pixels like the phone is a thermostat.

Fix it: Delete the #chips markup and its update code in index.html. Remove the offsets the hidden grid used to need. Consolidate the top position rules into one block.

heckles.message: v34: no-cache headers so phones load the new build
heckles.heckle:
You added no-cache, no-store headers to every path on the site, including images and scripts that never change, so every phone refetches everything on every visit. That is the cure for stale builds applied with a sledgehammer, and it is only needed because you keep pushing a new version number every twenty minutes. The landscape rules in index.html are a block of sixty pixel hand tuned sizes inside a max-height 330 media query, which will break on the first phone with a different notch. vercel.json is five lines and you still managed a blanket rule.

Fix it: Scope the no-cache header in vercel.json to the html file only. Give assets a versioned filename or normal caching. Replace the hand tuned landscape sizes in index.html with relative units.

heckles.message: Import accepts music_start and voice_start
heckles.heckle:
In server/app.py the import endpoint takes two more form fields and runs float(music_start or 0) on them, so a letter in the field throws a 500 instead of a clean 422. You changed the positional argument list for runner.run_experiment by adding two floats to the end, with no keyword names, so any other caller breaks without a sound. This service still has no auth on the job endpoint and wildcard CORS, and you keep adding inputs to it like piling more luggage on a bus with no brakes.

Fix it: Declare music_start and voice_start as float form fields with bounds in server/app.py so bad input gets a 422. Pass them to runner.run_experiment by keyword. Lock down CORS to your own origins. Add a shared key check on the import and start routes.

heckles.message: v23: Drive section on the launch menu with every ride, full ride lineup at the city home lot
heckles.heckle:
A trailer backing trainer now has a Drive section for every ride, because apparently the dockyard needed a sports car, a helicopter, an ambulance, and a van to teach anyone to back up a trailer. The EGGS table in index.html is a pile of hand typed coordinates and paint hex codes, one line of city spawn data per vehicle, so moving the lot means editing numbers by feel. The launch menu gets another section stacked into one dispatch card, which on a small screen is a scroll through a junk drawer. Focus left the building around version fourteen.

Fix it: Move the EGGS vehicle data in index.html into a named config with one entry per row, not a wall of literals. Group the Drive section behind its own screen instead of stacking it in the dispatch card. Decide what this app is and cut the rides that are not trailers.

heckles.message: Smash Bender queue carries music_start and voice_start
heckles.heckle:
This is the same two field change as the one you just made in the other repo, pasted here by hand, so now two repos must agree on a job shape and neither one has a schema. In api/bender.js the job takes music_start and voice_start with a Math.max and a Math.round wrapped around Number(b.music_start), but no upper limit, so someone can queue a job starting nine million seconds into a song. Your seconds field has a clamp of 10 to 240 and these two got nothing. Inconsistent, like a tax code.

Fix it: Clamp music_start and voice_start to a sane maximum in api/bender.js, the same way seconds is clamped. Write the job shape down once and share it between the repos. Reject jobs that are missing the video ids with a useful message. Add a rate limit on the queue action.

heckles.message: Smash Bender sends music_start and voice_start so both clips start lined up at the drop or the sample
heckles.heckle:
You are POSTing music_start and voice_start from index.html to an unauthenticated /api/bender queue that any stranger on the internet can fill, and the whole timing math lives in a new benderStarts function that has no test and returns rounded floats from a pile of optional arguments. The shell relay reads the values with jq and a quiet default of 0, so a bad value silently becomes zero and you get clips that are misaligned with no error. That is a campaign promise with a footnote. Also the failure message just says could not queue it, which tells nobody anything.

Fix it: Test benderStarts in index.html with a drop before, at, and after the start. Validate music_start and voice_start in tools/bender-relay.sh and fail loudly on garbage. Show the real error from the queue call. Put a shared secret on the queue endpoint.

heckles.message: v24: tank fire buttons get their own panel, truck only buttons hide while riding, side column scrolls
heckles.heckle:
You gave the tank its own fire panel pinned at bottom 200px, and made the side column scroll with the scrollbar hidden. So on a short phone in landscape, buttons slide off the bottom with no hint they exist. Hiding the scrollbar is hiding the evidence. The offsets are all magic numbers like 162px, 200px, and 262px stacked against each other, so one new button and the fire panel sits on top of the side column. Plan the layout like you plan a budget: badly and after the vote.

Fix it: Compute the side column height from the real layout in index.html instead of hard coded 162px, 200px, and 262px. Show a fade or arrow when #side can scroll. Use CSS variables for the shared offsets. Test it on a short landscape screen.

heckles.message: v25: driver view shows holes, craters, scorch, debris, marks, fire, smoke and flying chunks
heckles.heckle:
Driver view now draws holes, craters, scorch, debris, fire, smoke, and flying chunks, in one commit, in one file, with no profiling. The new line that builds colors for each object in the first person renderer is a nested ternary eleven deep, which is what a government shutdown looks like when written as code. Then you call fpHoleBoxes and fpDecals every frame, and for every wall with a breach you build fresh boxes, so a phone will turn into a hand warmer. Nobody asked whether the draw loop caches anything. Clearly not.

Fix it: Replace the object type color ternary in index.html with a lookup table. Cache the hole boxes per object until its damage changes. Cap the number of decals and debris pieces drawn per frame. Measure the frame time on an actual phone before adding more effects.

heckles.message: v26: chimes off, continuous engine voices for semi, tank, helicopter, cars and bike, noise tire screech
heckles.heckle:
You turned the chimes off by making tone() return early when the type is triangle. That is not a feature, that is a hack with a comment saying BLUE PHONE on it. Every future triangle sound silently dies and you will blame the browser. Then you added fifty lines of continuous engine oscillators and a noise screech with no sign of a cap on voices, so a phone with a weak audio thread will crackle like a town hall mic. Also the sound toggle is read from localStorage in a bare try block that swallows everything.

Fix it: Replace the triangle check in tone() in index.html with an explicit mute list by sound name. Cap the number of live engine voices and stop them when the ride changes. Add a master gain so you can turn the whole mess down. Log the swallowed localStorage error instead of hiding it.

heckles.message: v27: shells punch through light stuff and blast holes in walls, scorch and bullet pocks on walls, beeps removed
heckles.heckle:
Shells now punch through things and the damage state is stored in per area objects that pruneDmg filters on every call, with eleven chained filter clauses jammed on one line. That line is longer than a filibuster and twice as unreadable. You cut the gear shift beep and replaced it with a 70 hertz square thump, so the sound design is whatever you hummed this afternoon. You shipped a feature list longer than the test list, which is zero tests, because the game has none.

Fix it: Break the pruneDmg line in index.html into one statement per damage kind. Make the expiry times named constants instead of 1800 and 5400 sitting in the middle of a filter. Add a plain test that damage actually expires. Put the sound settings in one table instead of scattering tone calls.

heckles.message: Samples list: song names on their own line, buttons wrap below
heckles.heckle:
Three lines changed and you still found a way to do it badly. You added flex-wrap to .sampRow and then bolted on two rules keyed off the #sampList id, so the specificity war in index.html now has an ID selector holding a rifle. The font size of 10px on .seg buttons is a tap target for an ant, on a phone, where this thing is supposed to live. You fixed a cramped row by making the buttons smaller and calling it layout. That is a bailout with a press conference.

Fix it: Raise the .seg font size in index.html to at least 12px and give it a real minimum height for thumbs. Drop the #sampList prefix and use a class instead. Delete the dead .sampRow .rt flex rule that the new one overrides.

heckles.message: v28: tank rounds take chunks out of walls, smooth engine sound without blips, tire screech sound off
heckles.heckle:
Version twenty eight of a single index.html, and the title tag is still being bumped by hand like a kid updating a scoreboard with a marker. You are now carving craters out of walls with a tank in a trailer backing sim, which is mission creep worse than a defense appropriations bill. The new ret variable in the wall damage block is declared, assigned, and tangled into one line of semicolon soup that nobody, including you, can review. The RED PHONE and BLUE PHONE comments pile up in the header like campaign yard signs after the election.

Fix it: Split the hole carving code in index.html into named functions with real line breaks. Stop hand editing the title and read the version from one constant. Move the RED PHONE and BLUE PHONE history out of the head comment into a changelog file. Break the single file into modules before it hits ten thousand lines.

heckles.message: Comments open in a pop-up panel instead of filling each pad
heckles.heckle:
You made a pop-up sheet for comments and slapped it on server/static/index.html with .cmt using all: unset, which strips every default the browser gives a button. Then you pinned .sheet to the bottom with max-height: 40vh on the paragraph, so on a phone with the keyboard up your comment panel is a keyhole. This is a filibuster in CSS form: lots of talking, nothing visible. Also, you keep piling styles into one giant inline style block like the intern who never heard of a second file.

Fix it: Move the inline style block in server/static/index.html into its own stylesheet. Stop using all: unset on .cmt and .sheet .close and give them real focus and hit areas. Test .sheet on a small screen with the keyboard open. Close the sheet on Escape and on a tap outside it.

heckles.message: Sample log: stage three tab, Send to Auto-Tune, download button on every sample
heckles.heckle:
Stage three is a third copy of the tab you made an hour ago, wired by hand in server/static/index.html with another hardcoded button id. The tab row is a button with role tab and no arrow key handling, so the ARIA you copied is a campaign promise: sounds official, delivers nothing. Your stage names are now baked into three separate strings. Cereal box engineering, with a download link tacked on as a closing argument.

Fix it: Build the tabs in server/static/index.html from a stage array instead of pasting tab3. Add arrow key handling to the tablist or drop the tab roles. Keep stage names in one place shared with the server.

heckles.message: Processing API: Auto-Tune tool, stage three, stage limit
heckles.heckle:
In server/app.py send_stage2 you added a stage limit by reading the parent record and bailing at stage 3, and the endpoint is still called stage2. It parses int(body["run"]) twice with no guard, so a junk run value throws a 500 instead of the 400 you wrote for exactly this. CORS is wide open with allow_origins star on an endpoint that queues hour long jobs, so anyone on earth can burn your queue. Bailout level planning.

Fix it: Wrap the int conversion of run in send_stage2 in server/app.py and return a 400. Lock allow_origins to your own page. Rate limit or require a token on /api/stage2. Rename the endpoint or stop pretending it is stage two.

heckles.message: Auto-Tune tool (WORLD) and stage three: send any stage one or two sample to ElevenLabs or Auto-Tune
heckles.heckle:
server/autotune.py reads sys.argv by position like it is 1994, with the key, scale and speed as bare strings and no usage check, so a missing argument is a raw IndexError. Your key parsing falls back to root 0 when the name is unknown, so a typo in the key silently tunes everything to C. The stage2.py find_parent now does string splits on pipe characters to guess what kind of record it is, which is a government shutdown waiting for one experiment name with a pipe in it.

Fix it: Use argparse in server/autotune.py and reject an unknown key. Stop encoding record type in a pipe delimited string in find_parent in server/stage2.py and store a real field. Close the file handles in find_parent with a with block.

Another steward turn merged as one minified line in contrib/steward, five crosswalk hatches that each say in the meta that the steward completes the crosswalk. Completes it how, exactly, since the previous turns already drew crosswalks on the same streets? Nobody reviewed this PR, GitHub cannot even render a single line of JSON, and the whole process is a bailout machine printing coordinates at itself. Three of the five rectangles are near mirror copies with only the sign flipped.

Fix it: Pretty print the contrib json so diffs are reviewable. Have the steward check for existing crosswalk hatches before placing more. Validate duplicate geometry in the merge step instead of trusting the turn.

heckles.message: Experiment runs keep each sample's placed voice and music for stage two
heckles.heckle:
In server/experiment.py you shell out to cp to copy a wav you could copy with shutil, and you do it with check=True so one missing file kills the entire run. Then you write absolute paths for voice, instrument, acapella and reference into every log record, so the jsonl is welded to this one server's folder layout. Every sample now drags four paths around like campaign donors. The inst copy also happens once per stamp and never gets cleaned up, so disk fills quietly.

Fix it: Replace the cp subprocess in server/experiment.py with shutil.copyfile. Store paths relative to the data folder. Add cleanup for kept voice and inst files when an experiment is deleted.

heckles.message: Sample log: stage one and stage two tabs, Send to ElevenLabs on every sample
heckles.heckle:
You stuffed another 74 lines into server/static/index.html, which is now a single file doing tabs, trends, pads, ratings, sending and playback, held together with template strings. The .send button uses all: unset again and the disabled style only changes color, so on a bright phone screen a dead button looks alive. And you hardcoded the vendor into the button text, so every tool you add means editing markup like it is a hostage negotiation.

Fix it: Make the send button label come from the tool list returned by the server in index.html. Give the disabled .send a visible state beyond color. Split the script out of index.html. Escape every value you drop into a template string.

heckles.message: Stage two: send any sample to ElevenLabs for four refined versions, logged like stage one
heckles.heckle:
stage2.py opens jsonl files with bare open() in a loop and never closes them, and find_parent rescans every experiment file for each request, which is a full filesystem crawl to find one row. Worse, it calls an outside API with a key from the environment and the post endpoint in server/app.py has no auth at all and wildcard CORS, so any stranger can spend your credits. This is a bailout with a hole in the treasury.

Fix it: Add an auth check to /api/stage2 in server/app.py. Close files in stage2.find_parent with context managers. Index runs by key instead of rescanning every file per request. Cap queued jobs per hour.
